title: Cut-Sculpting Playbook — Console Backlog Grooming (Q3)
content:
Purpose:
This is a hands-on playbook for the Q3 console backlog cut exercise. The goal: reduce sprint noise by 25% and surface a tight set of high-impact, low-risk items we can ship in the next two sprints. This doc records the rubric, wireframe edits, per-ticket cut rationale, and action items (owner + ETA).

Scope and constraints:
- Scope: Console surface related to rollouts, routing, model selection, and the admin route editor (UI + light backend toggles). Not in scope: deep serving runtime work, infra autoscale changes, dedicated customer-only features.
- Constraint: Avoid introducing new server-side feature flags that require infra churn this quarter. Prefer client-side UI changes or wiring to existing APIs.
- Customer signals: CON-5123 (enterprise canary traffic tool) + several support threads (see linked artifacts).

Grooming agenda (60m):
1) Quick framing (5m) — review metrics and SLA target for next release
2) Rapid triage (25m) — apply rubric to 12 candidate tickets
3) Cut-sculpt (20m) — collapse/merge/defer per group decision
4) Assign owners & next steps (10m)

Triage rubric (applied as scores 1-5, lower is worse):
- User impact (1-5): number of customers or severity of pain
- Product leverage (1-5): unlocks other features or removes blockers
- Implementation effort (1-5): dev + design + QA rough estimate
- Risk/dependency (1-5): infra changes, cross-team coordination
- Observability & rollback friendliness (1-5): how easy to monitor and revert

Scoring guidance (quick):
- Items with (Impact >=4 and Effort <=3 and Risk <=3) are strong keepers
- Items with low impact (<=2) or high risk (>4) are candidates to defer

Cut-sculpt decisions (selected tickets discussed) — terse notes to capture reasoning:
1) CON-4789 "Route weight slider: fine-grained increments" — Keep (Score: Impact 4 / Effort 2 / Risk 2). Rationale: multiple customers asked for 1% granularity for canaries. Implementation: UI only + existing API hookup. Dev estimate: 2–3d. Wireframe note: slider needs alt-text and numeric input box. Owner: Liam.

2) CON-5011 "Model variant auto-fallback UI" — Defer (Score: Impact 3 / Effort 4 / Risk 4). Rationale: backend needs support for variant semantics; high infra coupling. Short-term alternative: add prominent docs + keyboard shortcut to switch variant. Action: add doc task (owner: Marisol).

3) CON-5066 "Route tagging & saved filters" — Keep, but split (Score: Impact 5 / Effort 5 / Risk 3). Rationale: high product leverage for platform teams but large scope. Split into: (a) minimal MVP: tag creation + single-filter list (Effort 2) — ship this sprint; (b) advanced saved filters & sharing (backlog). Owners: Devon (MVP), design for advanced.

4) CON-4902 "Rollout timeline visualization" — Cut this quarter (Score: Impact 3 / Effort 5 / Risk 3). Rationale: pretty but not necessary; would compete with core rollout controls. Defer until Q4 when we pair with metrics team.

5) CON-5140 "Keyboard-driven route editor (accessibility sprint)" — Keep (Score: Impact 4 / Effort 3 / Risk 1). Rationale: small effort, high accessibility win. Wireframe note: focus on command palette entry points + focus management. Estimate: 3d dev + 1d QA. Owner: Asha.

Wireframe / interaction notes (quick sketches converted to text):
- Route list row: add an overflow menu with a secondary action "quick canary" that opens an inline mini-editor (no full route nav). Rationale: reduces context switches.
- Canary editor modal: top row shows current % distribution with keyboard focus on numeric input; include microcopy: "Use arrows to nudge +/-1%" and an explicit "preview" that shows expected latency/cost delta (approx).
- Rollout toggle: replace binary switch with a three-state pill (off / staged / on) to better represent canary phases. Keep underlying API as before (meta only), no infra change.
- Accessibility: all interactive controls must expose aria-labels and a visible focus ring. Add a small e2e test in Cypress for TAB focus path.

Acceptance criteria (for items kept this sprint):
- CON-4789: slider supports 1% increments, numeric input syncs, keyboard arrows work, unit tests cover step change, integration smoke test to ensure API call shape unchanged.
- CON-5066 (MVP): create/delete tags, filter list by tag, tags persist in user prefs, no impact to backend schema.
- CON-5140: command palette entry, route editor fully keyboard-operable, AX test passes on screen reader basic flow.

Dev + QA estimates (rough):
- CON-4789 slider: 3 dev days + 1 qa day
- CON-5066 MVP tags: 5 dev days + 2 qa days (split across frontend + tiny backend storage hook)
- CON-5140 keyboard flows: 3 dev days + 1 qa day
Total: ~17 dev days across team, possible to distribute across two sprints if we stagger.

Risk mitigation / rollout plan:
- Feature flags: use existing UI flags (no infra feature flag creation). Ship behind user-pref flags where possible.
- Canary: for CON-5066 MVP, limit rollout to 10% of orgs first; monitor error rates and latency.
- Monitoring: add one simple dashboard tile per feature (errors per minute, API lat p95) and a PagerDuty runbook stub for obvious regressions.

Open questions (sticky items to resolve in async threads):
- Q1: For tags persistence, can we piggyback on user-settings service or do we need a new column? Action: @Devon to confirm with infra (#infra-ownership thread).
- Q2: Should the slider numeric input allow decimals for sub-1% experiments? We decided no for now.
- Q3: Design polish for three-state pill — do we use color alone? Need an accessibility-friendly pattern. @Marisol to propose two variants by 2026-07-08.

Notes to self / rough Slack links (for traceability):
- Slack: #console-product thread titled "cut-sculpt q3" (search) — contains customer quotes
- PR reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/789 (old prototype for slider)

Next steps (owners + ETA):
- Create trimmed ticket set for Sprint A (Liam) — due 2026-07-14
- Marisol to deliver pill design alternatives (2 variants) — due 2026-07-08
- Devon to confirm tags persistence approach with infra (post summary in #infra-ownership) — due 2026-07-07
- Asha to add keyboard flow tests and scaffold Cypress e2e (initial PR) — due 2026-07-18

Post-mortem / follow-up plan:
- After sprint close, run a 30-minute blameless review: what did we defer, what re-emerged as urgent, and did customer tickets improve? Capture outcomes in Confluence and link back to this doc.

Draft status: informal notes + wireframe snippets. Treat as the single source for Q3 console cut list until final grooming session.

-- end of playbook (notes saved from 2026-07-12 grooming session)"
